parsed.summary: This paper investigates whether temporal trajectories of routine biomarkers can predict pre-clinical functional mobility decline in older adults. Using data from 297,861 participants in the All of Us Research Program, the authors engineered trajectory features for twelve biomarkers and trained machine learning models. The LightGBM model incorporating trajectories achieved an AUROC of 0.797, significantly outperforming static baseline summaries and maintaining predictive signal up to 12 months before diagnosis.

chk_problem.value: Predicting pre-clinical functional mobility decline in older adults using longitudinal trajectories of routine biomarkers before observable impairment or falls occur.
chk_problem.paper_quote: A critical gap therefore exists: no large-scale study has systematically evaluated whether temporal trajectory features derived exclusively from routine laboratory measurements, without diagnosis codes, medications, or functional assessments, can predict pre-clinical functional decline.

chk_method.value: Feature engineering of longitudinal trajectory descriptors (mean, standard deviation, delta, count, linear slope) from twelve routine biomarkers, modeled using LightGBM and other machine learning algorithms.
chk_method.paper_quote: Trajectory features captured five per-biomarker descriptors: mean, standard deviation (intra-individual variability), delta (last minus first, directional change), count (measurement frequency), and linear slope (rate of change per day).

chk_data.value: A cohort of 297,861 participants (including 33,088 cases of mobility decline) from the All of Us Research Program Controlled Tier Dataset version 8.
chk_data.paper_quote: The primary modeling cohort contained 297,861 participants (33,088 cases, 11.1%).

chk_setup.value: Five-fold stratified cross-validation with out-of-fold predictions evaluated using AUROC and AUPRC, comparing four machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM).
chk_setup.paper_quote: All models were trained with 5-fold stratified cross-validation; out-of-fold (OOF) predictions across all folds were aggregated for unbiased evaluation.

chk_primary_result.value: LightGBM models incorporating trajectory features achieved an AUROC of 0.797 and an AUPRC of 0.380, significantly outperforming static baseline summaries.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: LightGBM models incorporating trajectories significantly outperformed static laboratory summaries (AUROC 0.797 vs. 0.755; DeLong p < 0.001; AUPRC 0.380 vs. 0.304).

chk_secondary_result.value: A prediction horizon analysis demonstrated sustained prediction of mobility decline 3 to 12 months before onset, with AUROCs ranging from 0.768 to 0.740.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: AUROC declined gradually from 0.768 at the 3-month horizon to 0.740 at the 12-month horizon, demonstrating that biomarker trajectories contain predictive signal up to one year before diagnosis (Table 2).

chk_baseline.value: Static laboratory summaries (baseline means) and demographics-only models.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: Baseline features used each biomarker’s mean value within the window.

chk_conclusion.value: Longitudinal trajectory features of routine biomarkers significantly improve the prediction of functional mobility decline, serving as a passive, zero-burden digital biomarker for early detection.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: Because the model relies exclusively on measurements already ordered in routine primary care, trajectory-based risk monitoring functions as a passive digital biomarker supporting equitable, zero-burden integration into EHR workflows for early detection of pre-clinical functional decline.

chk_limitation.value: Use of ICD-10 codes to define outcomes, high missingness in certain biomarkers, median imputation, cross-sectional splits, lack of comorbidity adjustment, and the need for external validation.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: ICD-10-coded outcomes capture documented recognition rather than objective functional performance, introducing potential detection bias.
